name: Cantabil Retail India Ltd
title: Cantabil Retail India Ltd - 533267 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Cantabil is a debt-free, self-funded men's apparel retailer; FY26 EBITDA margin 31% and gross margin ~60%, with 91 stores opened and 725 stores targeted in FY27, but no capacity-discipline signal and no price-hike plan beyond cost pass-through.

summary.headline: Cantabil FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 29% to INR264.3 crore at a 31% margin, with Q4 EBITDA up 34% to INR78.1 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 standalone revenue of INR852.6 crore (up 18%), PAT of INR95.8 crore (up 28%) and PAT margin of 11.2%. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 15% to INR253.5 crore, with EBITDA up 34% to INR78.1 crore and margin expanding to 30.8% from 26.6%. Management said same-store sales growth (SSG) was about 5% in FY26 and April 2026, and gross margin held near 60%. The company opened 91 stores in FY26 against 38 closures and relocations, and ended with 652 stores and 9.15 lakh sq ft.

segments.name: Company-operated (COCO) and franchise stores
segments.commentary: Network of 652 stores covering 9.15 lakh sq ft; about 80% COCO and 20% franchise, with franchise mainly in Tier 3 markets. Average new store size rose to about 1,400 sq ft in FY26 from about 1,100 sq ft three years ago.

segments.name: Online (e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 online revenue about INR11 crore vs about INR10 crore a year earlier (about 10% growth in value, about 13% in pieces per management). Management cited Myntra/Flipkart billing changes as a drag. A new 4-floor warehouse in the new corporate building serves online only.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Footwear sales were INR14 crore in FY26 vs INR10 crore in FY25 (+40%), about 2% of sales; target about 3-4% by end FY27, mainly via online.

segments.name: Kids wear
segments.commentary: About 2-3% of total sales; management expects 4-4.5% next year as family stores (45% of FY26 openings) grow.

segments.name: Manufacturing (Bahadurgarh)
segments.commentary: Own factory capacity of 18-20 lakh garments, meeting about 25% of requirement, with job workers at about 35%; the factory is a specialised suit plant. Management says the 60:40 own-and-job-work to accessories mix will broadly hold.

guidance_outlook: FY27 targets: about 725 stores and INR1,000 crore revenue; about 90-100 gross store additions (about 70-75% net).
Gross margin: internal target of about 60% maintained despite input cost inflation; EBITDA margin of about 30% expected if gross margin holds.
SSG guided at 5-6% for FY27, with upside to 7-8% described as too early to call.
Marketing spend about 1.7% of sales, could rise to 1.8-2%. Opex as a percentage of sales expected to stay within about plus or minus 1%.
Store area growth targeted at 15-20% per annum (15% minimum). Capex per sq ft expected to fall with a new furniture and fixture design; capex about INR1,800 per sq ft.
Lease cost: about INR99-100 crore in FY26 (Ind-AS 116 basis), rising to INR108-110 crore in FY27.
Corporate office and warehouse move expected to save INR1.5-2 crore annually from Q2/Q3 FY27.
Working capital about 105 days in FY26 (vs 115 days prior year); inventory days about 109-110, with target to keep below 120.
capex_capacity: FY26 openings: 91 stores (about 1.1 lakh sq ft added); 38 closures or relocations (about 24-25 renewals and relocations, 13 performance-based).
About 45 stores in the pipeline as of the call.
New corporate office and warehouse building (11 floors; 4 for corporate, 4 for online warehousing, WMS-automated) is capitalised; building cost about INR50-55 crore excluding land.
Company is debt free and funds capex from internal accruals; about INR100 crore of capex has been planned, with a further expansion plan expected from Q3 FY27.
Bahadurgarh factory floor expansion is under way (part of INR10 crore CWIP). Management said manufacturing will rely more on job workers than on a new own plant.
Nepal: four stores (mix of multi-brand and EBO), run through a selling and distribution model; no other overseas markets yet.
demand_pricing: SSG about 5% in FY26 and in April 2026; May 2026 SSG described as decent. Management says it is on track for 5-6% even if rates rise by about 100 bps.

Average bill value up about 10% a year, attributed to inflation plus better product mix. Management did not share price-hike plans beyond saying prices depend on cost, with some input cost passed on to customers.
Q4 gross margin of about 57% (vs 53-54% a year earlier) was attributed to product mix, pricing correction and GST benefit.
Management says footfall is holding up with no impact seen yet from inflation.
Retail cost fell to 33% of sales from 34%. Backend corporate cost about 8% of sales.
Average rent per sq ft fell to INR115 in FY26 from INR120. Inventory above 1 year is about 25-30% of total; provisioning is 10% for 1-3 years and 50% above 3 years.
Management said it will not enter fast fashion (Zara-type) and will stay with basic and collection-led brands such as UNIQLO.

qa_highlights.question: Is SSG correlated with monetary policy, and what levers exist if rates rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SSG was about 5% in FY26 and in April 2026, and it expects to keep 5-6% even if rates rise about 100 bps, citing incentives, efficiency and marketing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is INR25 crore shown under loans?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an intercorporate loan to a non-related party at about 12% for one year, versus market returns of 6-7% on surplus funds; management said it could be closed in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the lease cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Lease cash outflow (principal plus interest, Ind-AS 116) was about INR100 crore in FY26; actual rental cost was about INR99 crore. It is expected to rise to INR108-110 crore in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross margin of 60% sustainable in FY27 despite input inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 60% gross margin is an internal target, with about 1% variance either way.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 gross margin of about 57%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited product mix, pricing correction and GST benefit, not procurement efficiency, and said the margin will be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Is online growing, and how is it measured?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 online revenue was about INR11 crore vs INR9.9-10 crore a year earlier (about 10% in value and 13% in pieces). The platforms changed billing, which reduced reported value growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory and working capital position?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital was about 105 days in FY26 (vs 115 days), inventory days about 109-110; management expects it to stay around this level.

risks_watch: Inflation and possible monetary tightening could reduce discretionary demand; management has not quantified the sensitivity.
Input cost pressure may hit gross margin, which management targets at about 60%; Q4 FY26 margin was flattered by mix and GST.
Store-addition pace: FY26 gross openings of 91 were above the plan, but the 675-store plan was missed on net count as closures and relocations offset openings.
Online channel growth lags the platform headline (about 10% in value vs 13% in pieces) because of billing changes at Myntra and Flipkart.
Deployment of surplus cash: INR25 crore is in a non-related intercorporate loan, and the company has not yet announced a specific expansion plan for the cash.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 records, growth and margin targets. Answers on SSG, gross margin and opex were direct; answers on FY28 inflation planning and the cash deployment plan were vaguer.
key_quotes: The margin, what we are targeting on a long-term basis is approximately 60%.
The moment we will be able to maintain that, our EBITDA margin, 30% will always be on the card.
We are targeting that 15% to 20%, 15% minimum.
Interest cost, we don't have because we are debt free.

FY27 gross store additions of 90-100 (about 70-75% net), targeting 725 stores total
Store area growth targeted at 15-20% per annum (15% minimum) with capex about INR1,800 per sq ft; about INR100 crore capex planned
New corporate office and warehouse building (11 floors, WMS-automated), capitalised; building cost about INR50-55 crore excluding land

growth.why: FY27 guidance of about INR1,000 crore revenue (about 17% growth on FY26's INR852.6 crore), 725 stores via 90-100 gross additions, and 5-6% SSG; backed by 91 stores opened in FY26, about 45 in pipeline and about INR100 crore capex planned, though no order-book style quantification of demand beyond SSG history.
